ballot: Democrats have won 256 seats to Republicans' 169, with 10 races still uncalled — 38 above the 218 needed for a majority (AP count as of Nov. 14, via California Today)
senate: Democrats hold 55 seats after Scott Colom's win in Mississippi (AP, Nov. 11). In Alaska, Mary Peltola leads Dan Sullivan 49.94% to 45.96%, about 11,200 votes, just short of a majority; ranked-choice tabulation is due on Nov. 18 (Alaska Division of Elections results, via Newsweek, Nov. 16)
approval: 36% approve, 61% disapprove among registered voters in this week's Economist/YouGov poll, tied for his lowest in either term (YouGov, via Opinion Today, Nov. 15). Reuters/Ipsos had 32% approve, 65% disapprove (Nov. 6–9)
ledger_source: AP count via California Today (Nov. 14), Alaska Division of Elections via Newsweek (Nov. 16), Economist/YouGov via Opinion Today (Nov. 15), Reuters/Ipsos via Yahoo News (Nov. 6–9)

headlines.headline: Colom defeats Hyde-Smith in Mississippi
headlines.short: Colom wins Mississippi, the first Democratic senator there since 1989.
headlines.summary: Democrat Scott Colom beat Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith 49.2% to 48.7%, a race separated by 65 votes on election night; Hyde-Smith conceded on Nov. 11. Colom is Mississippi's first Democratic senator since 1989 and the first Black candidate elected to the Senate from the state in more than 140 years. Democrats now hold 55 Senate seats.

headlines.headline: Peltola closes in on 50% in Alaska
headlines.short: Alaska: Peltola leads Sullivan by 11,200 votes; ranked-choice count Nov. 18.
headlines.summary: The latest Alaska Division of Elections figures give Democrat Mary Peltola 140,637 first-choice votes (49.94%) to Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan's 129,424 (45.96%), a lead of 11,213, leaving her just short of a majority. If no one passes 50%, ranked-choice tabulation begins on Nov. 18. The AP has not called the race; it estimated 97% of the vote counted on Sunday.

headlines.headline: Inside Stephen Miller's first week as chief of staff
headlines.short: Miller moves fast to take control as Trump's new chief of staff.
headlines.summary: In his first week replacing Susie Wiles, Stephen Miller moved to consolidate control of the White House and signalled changes to procedures and personnel. Two memos, presented as empowering Cabinet secretaries and limiting lobbyists, were widely read as criticism of how Wiles ran the first two years. CNN's reporting, summarised by Political Wire.

headlines.headline: Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader
headlines.short: Jordan beats Scalise 106–73 to lead House Republicans in the minority.
headlines.summary: House Republicans chose Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress, 106 votes to 73 over Majority Leader Steve Scalise, after Speaker Mike Johnson said he would not run. Tom Emmer becomes minority whip. In the Senate, John Thune was re-elected Republican leader.

headlines.headline: House sidelines Hegseth impeachment
headlines.short: House votes 211–204 to send Hegseth impeachment to committee.
headlines.summary: Republican Thomas Massie's articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, over the Iran war, strikes on alleged drug boats, the capture of Nicolás Maduro without congressional approval and the move against Sen. Mark Kelly, were referred to committee by 211 votes to 204, effectively ending the effort this session. Hakeem Jeffries, expected to be the next Speaker, said Hegseth "has got to go".

podcasts.summary: "Susie Wiles Out, Stephen Miller In: What is Trump Thinking?" (Nov 9) — Katty Kay and Anthony Scaramucci on Miller's first moves as chief of staff, Trump's first interview after the midterms, and what Democrats should prioritise in Congress.
"Is this the end of the Trump era?" (Nov 6) — The Economist's US team asks whether the midterms end a decade of Trump's dominance, and how Democrats might use their new power.

wildcard: Gavin Newsom says he'll decide on a 2028 run "at the beginning of the year" — telling Turkey's Anadolu news agency at the UN climate summit in Antalya.

context: A week of disruption beyond Washington politics. On Friday 13 November the FAA halted every departure in the country for more than four hours after radar and communications failures; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed outdated equipment and asked Congress for billions to modernise air traffic control, and Democrats promised hearings. A day earlier Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia, the chipmaker at the centre of the AI boom, after the board began investigating reports that he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort; finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO. And on Thursday 19 November Trump is due to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, the first formal three-way meeting of US, Chinese and Russian leaders, with nuclear arms and the Iran war on the agenda.
